body:
## Problem

`WorldCore::restore` (`pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs`) validates a journal entry's author for some entry kinds but not for the events that carry the world's content:

- `JournalEntry::Issued` refuses a parent that was never issued (core.rs:184-188), and `JournalEntry::Revoked` refuses an unknown or already-revoked participant (core.rs:225-230).
- `JournalEntry::Committed` (core.rs:320-355) checks only the sequence (`event.sequence == core.sequence + 1`). It never checks `event.participant_id`.
- `JournalEntry::Checkpoint` (core.rs:360-430) validates its events' sequences (consecutive, last equals the checkpoint sequence) but never their `participant_id`s either.

Restore's own contract is that a journal "is internally inconsistent (out-of-order sequences, **unknown participants**, malformed digests). A bad journal is refused, never partially applied" (core.rs:130-133).

Live code can only produce a `Committed` event from participant 0 (the host: `system_chat`, core.rs:578, journaled as Committed at actor.rs:706-709; `ProgramInstalled`, actor.rs:1283) or from a participant issued in the same journal (`chat`/`prepare_input` authorize a capability first). A `Committed` event naming any other participant ID — one never issued, or issued only *later* in the journal — is a shape no live path produces, yet restore accepts it:

1. **Ghost inputs are replayed into the program.** A `Committed` `Input` from a never-issued participant is pushed onto `replay` (core.rs:342), and `open_world` (world_store.rs:380) feeds replay through the re-instantiated program — the program executes an input no participant ever sent, and the use-count accounting that live input passes (`ensure_uses_left`, then `spend`) is skipped entirely for the ghost (`commit_prepared`'s `spend` walks the capability chain; an unknown ID spends nothing).
2. **Ghost chat is retained and projected to real participants.** A `Committed` `Chat` from a never-issued participant is stored in the retained events and appears in snapshots / `events_after` projections for legitimate participants, attributed to a participant ID that is not in the snapshot's participant list.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `690e4722`; laptop probe at 8b89d14a2, `core.rs` md5-identical)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-laneB-restorepart/`, a detached worktree of `origin/main`; integration test `pkgs/id/tests/probe_restorepart.rs` against the real `id` crate, token digests built exactly as `mint` builds them):

- CONTROL: `Created` + `Issued(1, GUEST)` + `Committed(seq 1, participant 1, Input)` restores `Ok`, replay length 1.
- CONTROL: `Created` + `Committed(seq 1, participant 0, Chat)` (host line) restores `Ok`.
- CASE A: `Created` + `Issued(1)` + `Committed(seq 1, participant 999, Input)` — participant 999 was never issued — restores `Ok`; the ghost input is in `replay` (participant 999), and `core.participant(999)` is `None`.
- CASE B: same journal with `Chat` from participant 999 restores `Ok`; a snapshot taken with participant 1's legitimate token lists participants `[1]` but its events contain the chat line attributed to participant 999.
- CASE C: a `Checkpoint` whose retained events name participant 999 restores `Ok`.

## Why it matters

Restore is the trust boundary for persisted world state (journals are copied by fork, moved between hosts, and read after crashes/torn writes — `world_store.rs` `open_world`). Every neighbouring arm of restore treats an unknown participant as a fatal inconsistency; the two arms carrying actual user content (inputs that drive the program, chat that other participants read) are the ones that skip the check. An input replayed from a nonexistent participant changes program state and published records with no accountable author and no use-limit accounting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore refuses a `Committed` event whose `participant_id` is neither 0 (host) nor a participant issued earlier in the same journal, with an error naming the participant and sequence, in the style of the neighbouring restore errors.
- [ ] Restore refuses a `Checkpoint` whose retained events name a participant that is neither 0 nor issued before the checkpoint.
- [ ] Legitimate journals still restore: host (participant 0) chat and `ProgramInstalled` events, issued participants' chat/inputs, and existing checkpoint/fork fixtures.
- [ ] Regression tests beside the existing restore tests (cf. `restore_refuses_a_delegate_outliving_its_parent`): ghost input refused, ghost chat refused, ghost checkpoint event refused, host + issued controls pass.
- [ ] Triage pins the rule for an event naming a participant issued *later* in the journal (the live order is always issue-then-commit, so "issued earlier" is the natural reading) and for an event by a participant revoked earlier in the journal (live chat/input is refused after revocation via `authorize`, but the event was legitimately committed before the revoke in a real journal — confirm restored historical events by since-revoked participants stay valid).

Dedup checked this run: open+closed search for world journal restore / unknown participant — #2890 (restore never validates `Issued` *scopes*; same function, different entry arm and different invariant, filed by Lane A this hour — cross-linked, not a duplicate), #2093/#1598 (world-doctor journal-check disagreements, different surface), #1403 (replay omits chat, opposite direction). No filing covers event-author validation in restore.
